q: The pain is caused by an acid called ____.
e: The pain is caused by an acid called methanoic (formic) acid. Methanoic (formic) acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The pain we sometimes feel in our leg muscles during exercise is caused by ____.
e: The pain we sometimes feel in our leg muscles during exercise is caused by lactic acid. Sore muscles after hard exercise are linked to lactic acid building up.

q: Our stomach produces an acid (____) for food digestion.
e: Our stomach produces an acid (HCl) for food digestion. HCl is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ordinary battery acid is ____.
e: Ordinary battery acid is sulphuric acid. Sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acid is a substance which when dissolved in water produces ____.
e: Acid is a substance which when dissolved in water produces hydrogen ions (H+). An acid produces hydrogen ions, H+, when it dissolves in water. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: In other words, an acid increases the number of ____ ions in an aqueous solution.
e: In other words, an acid increases the number of H+ ions in an aqueous solution. H+ is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Base is a substance which when dissolved in water produces ____.
e: Base is a substance which when dissolved in water produces hydroxide ions (OH-). Hydroxide ions (OH-) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In other words, a base increases the concentration of ____ ions in an aqueous solution.
e: In other words, a base increases the concentration of OH- ions in an aqueous solution. OH- is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many 'acids' are ____, meaning they destroy body tissue and clothing and many are also poisonous.
e: Many 'acids' are corrosive, meaning they destroy body tissue and clothing and many are also poisonous. Corrosive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some organic acids are used in food preservative, food fermentation, salad, etc., such as ____.
e: Some organic acids are used in food preservative, food fermentation, salad, etc., such as ethanoic acid (acetic acid). Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The word 'acid' comes from the Latin word acidus, which means ____.
e: The word 'acid' comes from the Latin word acidus, which means sour. Sour is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acids can be classified as mineral acids (inorganic acids) and ____ acids.
e: Acids can be classified as mineral acids (inorganic acids) and organic acids. Organic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When a strong acid dissolves in water, it ____ dissociates to produce hydrogen ions, which are protons, ($H^+$), and a weak acid only partially dissociates in water.
e: When a strong acid dissolves in water, it completely dissociates to produce hydrogen ions, which are protons, (H+), and a weak acid only partially dissociates in water. A strong acid dissociates almost completely in water.

q: Mineral acids are strong acids and organic acids are ____ acids.
e: Mineral acids are strong acids and organic acids are weak acids. A weak acid dissociates only partly in water.

q: Caution: Always add strong acid slowly to ____.
e: Caution: Always add strong acid slowly to water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An acid is a compound which becomes a ____ donor when dissolved in water.
e: An acid is a compound which becomes a proton (H+) donor when dissolved in water. A proton sits in the nucleus and carries a positive charge.

q: Acids are hazardous, irritant and ____.
e: Acids are hazardous, irritant and corrosive. Corrosive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acids have a ____ taste.
e: Acids have a sour taste. Sour is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acids dissolve in water to form solutions which conduct ____.
e: Acids dissolve in water to form solutions which conduct electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acid solutions have pH values less than ____.
e: Acid solutions have pH values less than 7. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: Acids have the ability to change the colour of indicators and turn blue litmus paper (an indicator) ____.
e: Acids have the ability to change the colour of indicators and turn blue litmus paper (an indicator) red. Red is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acid reacts with metals to form a salt and ____.
e: Acid reacts with metals to form a salt and hydrogen. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: Acid reacts with metal oxides and hydroxides to form a salt and ____ only.
e: Acid reacts with metal oxides and hydroxides to form a salt and water only. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acid reacts with carbonate to form a salt, ____ and water.
e: Acid reacts with carbonate to form a salt, carbon dioxide and water. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used in extraction of some metals such as copper, manufacture of fertilisers, detergents, paints, rubber, paper and pulp industry, car batteries and rust removal.
e: Sulphuric acid is used in extraction of some metals such as copper, manufacture of fertilisers, detergents, paints, rubber, paper and pulp industry, car batteries and rust removal. Sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used to help swimming pools be free of algae, to make aqua regia for dissolving gold and platinum.
e: Hydrochloric acid is used to help swimming pools be free of algae, to make aqua regia for dissolving gold and platinum. Hydrochloric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: aqua regia is a mixture of one part of the concentrated ____ acid and three parts of the concentrated hydrochloric acid.
e: Aqua regia is a mixture of one part of the concentrated nitric acid and three parts of the concentrated hydrochloric acid. Nitric is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is used in making fertilisers and explosives, to make aqua regia for dissolving gold and platinum.
e: Nitric acid is used in making fertilisers and explosives, to make aqua regia for dissolving gold and platinum. Nitric is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is used in making fertilisers and rust inhibitor.
e: Phosphoric acid is used in making fertilisers and rust inhibitor. Phosphoric is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is used in fizzy drinks.
e: Carbonic acid is used in fizzy drinks. Carbonic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is used in fruit juices, in the preparation of effervescent salts, as a food preservative.
e: Citric acid is used in fruit juices, in the preparation of effervescent salts, as a food preservative. Citric is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is used in vinegar, used in salad dressings.
e: Ethanoic acid is used in vinegar, used in salad dressings. Ethanoic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A ____ reaction is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks apart into two or more parts.
e: A dissociation reaction is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks apart into two or more parts. Dissociation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ acid is an acid that completely dissociates in water and gives $H^+$ ions.
e: Strong acid is an acid that completely dissociates in water and gives H+ ions. A strong acid dissociates almost completely in water.

q: ____ acid is an acid that partially dissociates in aqueous solution and gives $H^+$ ions.
e: Weak acid is an acid that partially dissociates in aqueous solution and gives H+ ions. A weak acid dissociates only partly in water.

q: An acid solution which contains the pure acid or predominantly large proportion of the acid is called ____ acid.
e: An acid solution which contains the pure acid or predominantly large proportion of the acid is called concentrated acid. Concentrated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An acid solution which contains a relatively small amount of the acid is called ____ acid.
e: An acid solution which contains a relatively small amount of the acid is called dilute acid. Dilute is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bases and alkalis are found in many ____ agents such as soap and many household detergents.
e: Bases and alkalis are found in many cleaning agents such as soap and many household detergents. Cleaning is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When wood ashes are burnt, the product is ____.
e: When wood ashes are burnt, the product is alkaline. Alkaline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The word alkali comes from the Arabic 'al-qili' which means ____.
e: The word alkali comes from the Arabic 'al-qili' which means burnt ashes. Burnt ashes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A base is usually a metallic oxide or hydroxide and will react with an acid to form a salt and ____ only.
e: A base is usually a metallic oxide or hydroxide and will react with an acid to form a salt and water only. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An alkali is a base that is ____ in water.
e: An alkali is a base that is soluble in water. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

q: Alkalis can be strong or ____.
e: Alkalis can be strong or weak. Weak is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Strong alkalis dissolve in water to produce ____ ions in solution.
e: Strong alkalis dissolve in water to produce OH- ions in solution. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

q: Sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide are examples of ____ alkalis.
e: Sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide are examples of strong alkalis. Strong is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ammonium hydroxide is the most common example of a ____ alkali.
e: Ammonium hydroxide is the most common example of a weak alkali. Weak is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most bases are ____ in water.
e: Most bases are insoluble in water. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: MgO, CuO, $Fe_2O_3$, etc. are ____ bases.
e: MgO, CuO, Fe2O3, etc. are insoluble bases. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Strong bases are ____ to handle.
e: Strong bases are hazardous to handle. Hazardous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bases have a ____ taste and soapy feel.
e: Bases have a bitter taste and soapy feel. Bitter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bases cause a colour change in indicators. Litmus changes from red to ____ in a basic solution.
e: Bases cause a colour change in indicators. Litmus changes from red to blue in a basic solution. Blue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alkalis have pH values greater than ____.
e: Alkalis have pH values greater than 7. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: Bases react with acids to ____ each other and form a salt and water.
e: Bases react with acids to neutralise each other and form a salt and water. Neutralise is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When alkalis are gently warmed with ammonium salt, the products include a salt, water and ____.
e: When alkalis are gently warmed with ammonium salt, the products include a salt, water and ammonia. Ammonia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alkalis react with fatty acids to form ____.
e: Alkalis react with fatty acids to form soaps. Turning fat into soap is an old chemical change, a kind of saponification.

q: ____ is used in making soap, paper, baking soda, oven cleaners.
e: Sodium hydroxide is used in making soap, paper, baking soda, oven cleaners. Sodium hydroxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used in treating acidic soil (liming), making cement, limewater, mortar, plaster.
e: Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is used in treating acidic soil (liming), making cement, limewater, mortar, plaster. Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used in making cement (quicklime).
e: Calcium oxide is used in making cement (quicklime). Calcium oxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used in antacids (gastric medicine), in toothpaste.
e: Magnesium oxide is used in antacids (gastric medicine), in toothpaste. Magnesium oxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is used in many household cleaners and production of ammonia fertilisers.
e: NH4OH is used in many household cleaners and production of ammonia fertilisers. NH4OH is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A base or an alkali is a chemical compound that combines with an acid to form a salt and ____.
e: A base or an alkali is a chemical compound that combines with an acid to form a salt and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An alkali is a base which is soluble in water producing ____ ions.
e: An alkali is a base which is soluble in water producing OH- ions. OH- is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All alkalis are bases but all bases are not ____.
e: All alkalis are bases but all bases are not alkalis. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

q: A strong base is a base that ____ dissociates in water producing $OH^-$ ions.
e: A strong base is a base that completely dissociates in water producing OH- ions. Completely is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A weak base is a base that ____ dissociates in water producing $OH^-$ ions.
e: A weak base is a base that partially dissociates in water producing OH- ions. Partially is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many brightly coloured flowers, vegetables and berries make good ____.
e: Many brightly coloured flowers, vegetables and berries make good indicators. An indicator changes colour to show whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

q: the coloured juice extracted from red cabbage is ____ in acids and green in alkalis.
e: The coloured juice extracted from red cabbage is pink in acids and green in alkalis. Pink is the idea that completes this fact.

q: the coloured juice extracted from red cabbage is pink in acids and ____ in alkalis.
e: The coloured juice extracted from red cabbage is pink in acids and green in alkalis. Green is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrangea flowers are interesting natural indicators. They are ____ when grown in acidic soil and pink or red when grown in alkaline soil.
e: Hydrangea flowers are interesting natural indicators. They are blue when grown in acidic soil and pink or red when grown in alkaline soil. Blue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrangea flowers are interesting natural indicators. They are blue when grown in acidic soil and pink or red when grown in ____ soil.
e: Hydrangea flowers are interesting natural indicators. They are blue when grown in acidic soil and pink or red when grown in alkaline soil. Alkaline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Indicators are dyes, or a mixture of dyes, which change ____ when they are added to acids or alkalis.
e: Indicators are dyes, or a mixture of dyes, which change colour when they are added to acids or alkalis. Colour is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Litmus is red in acidic solution, ____ in neutral and blue in alkaline solution.
e: Litmus is red in acidic solution, purple in neutral and blue in alkaline solution. Purple is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Litmus is red in acidic solution, purple in neutral and ____ in alkaline solution.
e: Litmus is red in acidic solution, purple in neutral and blue in alkaline solution. Blue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the solution is known as ____.
e: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the solution is known as pH. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: The pH value can be measured by ____.
e: The pH value can be measured by pH meter. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: It is a much more reliable and accurate method of measuring pH than the ____ paper.
e: It is a much more reliable and accurate method of measuring pH than the universal indicator paper. An indicator changes colour to show whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

q: Acidic conditions in the stomach (pH~____) are needed for good digestion.
e: Acidic conditions in the stomach (pH~1.5) are needed for good digestion. 1.5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Usually the body maintains the pH of blood close to ____.
e: Usually the body maintains the pH of blood close to 7.4. 7.4 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions with pH below 7 are ____.
e: Solutions with pH below 7 are acidic. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: Solutions with pH above 7 are ____.
e: Solutions with pH above 7 are basic. Basic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions with pH equal to 7 are ____.
e: Solutions with pH equal to 7 are neutral. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: Highly acidic soil is treated by spreading quicklime (CaO), slaked lime ($Ca(OH)_2$) or calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$) to lower its ____.
e: Highly acidic soil is treated by spreading quicklime (CaO), slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) or calcium carbonate (CaCO3) to lower its acidity. Acidity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Highly alkaline soil is treated by adding gypsum ($CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$) to lower its ____.
e: Highly alkaline soil is treated by adding gypsum (CaSO4 2H2O) to lower its alkalinity. Alkalinity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An indicator is a substance that has different ____ in acidic and alkaline solutions.
e: An indicator is a substance that has different colours in acidic and alkaline solutions. An indicator changes colour to show whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

q: The pH of pure water is ____.
e: The pH of pure water is 7. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: The sea water contains many salts such as ____, potassium chloride, magnesium sulphate, magnesium chloride and magnesium bromide.
e: The sea water contains many salts such as sodium chloride, potassium chloride, magnesium sulphate, magnesium chloride and magnesium bromide. Sodium chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (____), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc.
e: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc. Epsom salt is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (____), etc.
e: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc. Limestone is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A salt is produced when an acid reacts with a ____.
e: A salt is produced when an acid reacts with a base. A base reacts with an acid to give a salt and water.

q: The salt consists of two parts. One part comes from the base, the other from the ____.
e: The salt consists of two parts. One part comes from the base, the other from the acid. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The sodium ion ($Na^+$) part of the salt comes from the base and the chloride ion ($Cl^-$) comes from the ____.
e: The sodium ion (Na+) part of the salt comes from the base and the chloride ion (Cl-) comes from the acid. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt and water are formed. This reaction is known as ____.
e: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt and water are formed. This reaction is known as neutralisation. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water.

q: It involves the combination of $H^+$ ion produced from acid and $OH^-$ ion produced from base to form ____.
e: It involves the combination of H+ ion produced from acid and OH- ion produced from base to form water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Neutralisation reaction occurs in our stomach. The acid (HCl) produced by our stomach, is so strong that it is ____ with a base produced by cells.
e: Neutralisation reaction occurs in our stomach. The acid (HCl) produced by our stomach, is so strong that it is neutralised with a base produced by cells. Neutralised is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Salts are also produced when an acid reacts with a metal or a metal ____.
e: Salts are also produced when an acid reacts with a metal or a metal carbonate. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: hydrochloric acid HCl produces ____ salts.
e: Hydrochloric acid HCl produces chloride salts. Chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sulphuric acid $H_2SO_4$ produces ____ salts.
e: Sulphuric acid H2SO4 produces sulphate salts. Sulphate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: nitric acid $HNO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Nitric acid HNO3 produces nitrate salts. Nitrate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sulphurous acid $H_2SO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Sulphurous acid H2SO3 produces sulphite salts. Sulphite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: carbonic acid $H_2CO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: Carbonic acid H2CO3 produces carbonate salts. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ethanoic acid $CH_3COOH$ produces ____ salt.
e: Ethanoic acid CH3COOH produces ethanoate salt. Ethanoate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all ____ are soluble.
e: All nitrates are soluble. Nitrates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all chlorides are soluble except silver, mercury(I), ____.
e: All chlorides are soluble except silver, mercury(I), lead(II). Lead(II) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: all sulphates are soluble except ____, lead(II), calcium.
e: All sulphates are soluble except barium, lead(II), calcium. Barium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: carbonates of sodium, potassium and ____ are soluble.
e: Carbonates of sodium, potassium and ammonium are soluble. Ammonium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The preparation method depends on whether the salt is ____ in water or not.
e: The preparation method depends on whether the salt is soluble in water or not. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Soluble salts are usually prepared by crystallisation method. Crystallisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by precipitation method. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: Salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium can be prepared from caustic soda solution (NaOH), caustic potash solution (KOH) and ammonia solution ($NH_4OH$), respectively, by the ____ using the appropriate acid.
e: Salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium can be prepared from caustic soda solution (NaOH), caustic potash solution (KOH) and ammonia solution (NH4OH), respectively, by the neutralisation using the appropriate acid. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water.

q: Insoluble salts are prepared by ____.
e: Insoluble salts are prepared by precipitation. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: A ____ precipitate of barium sulphate, $BaSO_4$, is formed.
e: A white precipitate of barium sulphate, BaSO4, is formed. White is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sodium chloride NaCl is used as a food ____.
e: Sodium chloride NaCl is used as a food additive. Additive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: sodium sulphate $Na_2SO_4$, sodium nitrite $NaNO_2$, sodium citrate $Na_3C_6H_5O_7$ are used as food ____.
e: Sodium sulphate Na2SO4, sodium nitrite NaNO2, sodium citrate Na3C6H5O7 are used as food preservatives. Preservatives is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ammonium sulphate $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, ammonium nitrate $NH_4NO_3$, ammonium phosphate $(NH_4)_3PO_4$ are used as ____.
e: Ammonium sulphate (NH4)2SO4, ammonium nitrate NH4NO3, ammonium phosphate (NH4)3PO4 are used as fertilisers. Fertilisers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: potassium chloride KCl is used as a ____.
e: Potassium chloride KCl is used as a fertiliser. Fertiliser is the idea that completes this fact.

q: magnesium sulphate $MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O$ is used for medical uses (____).
e: Magnesium sulphate MgSO4 7H2O is used for medical uses (Epsom salt). Epsom salt is the idea that completes this fact.

q: magnesium hydroxide $Mg(OH)_2$ is used for medical uses (____, MOM).
e: Magnesium hydroxide Mg(OH)2 is used for medical uses (milk of magnesia, MOM). Milk of magnesia is the idea that completes this fact.

q: calcium sulphate $CaSO_4$ is used for medical uses (____, POP).
e: Calcium sulphate CaSO4 is used for medical uses (Plaster of Paris, POP). Plaster of Paris is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A salt is a substance produced from the reaction between an acid and a base or a ____.
e: A salt is a substance produced from the reaction between an acid and a base or a metal. Metal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Based on the ____, salts can be classified as chlorides, sulphates, nitrates, sulphites and carbonates, etc.
e: Based on the acids, salts can be classified as chlorides, sulphates, nitrates, sulphites and carbonates, etc. Acids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared from the reactions between metals and dilute acids followed by ____.
e: Soluble salts are usually prepared from the reactions between metals and dilute acids followed by crystallisation. Crystallisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and ____ only.
e: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water only. Water is the idea that completes this fact.
